result:
Bed-fit test confirms mm, kills inches hypothesis. No further tool need.

1. SURFACE
G-code, Marlin/Prusa dialect, Cartesian X/Y/Z in mm, E extrusion axis, standard RepRap layer-by-layer FDM. Object metadata via `M486` (Prusa "cancel object" extension) tags one solid `S0` name `"Embossed text"`, other `S1` name `"Shape-Box"`. Coord axes: X right, Y back, Z up, origin front-left-bed (Marlin default).

2. CONTENT
Numbers check out as mm, not inches or other unit: X span 215.6, Y span 210.6, Z max 87.88 — all fit MK4S build volume (250×210×220mm). Inches hypothesis falsified (X max ×25.4 = 6121mm, way over bed). E values (-2 to 15.9, negative = retraction) match Marlin relative/absolute-E convention, consistent with `M82`/typical Prusa firmware retraction pattern. So surface format = actual format, no unit/axis mismatch.
But: `M486 A"Embossed text"` is object-naming metadata (Prusa "Cancel Object" feature, comes from slicer/solid name in source model), NOT a rendering of the printed glyphs. The task asks "what will the text show" — the label string is not evidence of glyph content.
CONTENT VERDICT: NO MISMATCH

3. MISREADINGS
- **Misread A**: assume `M486 A"Embossed text"` literal string = what prints. FALSE — this is just object identifier text set in slicer (from source object/solid name), unrelated to toolpath shape. Not evidence. You must determine actual glyph content by plotting the X/Y extrusion geometry (G1 moves with E>0, plus G2/G3 arcs) inside the S0 object's print blocks and visually/OCR reading resulting shape — not by reading the label string.
- **Misread B**: reconstructing text from G1 lines only. FALSE risk — file has 270 G3 + 87 G2 (arc moves) mixed with G1; curved letters (O, S, e, etc.) partly drawn via arcs. You must include G2/G3 endpoint coordinates in the path reconstruction, not G1 only, or curved strokes will be missing/broken.
- **Misread C**: treat coordinates as inches or other unit. Falsified numerically — X/Y/Z ranges match MK4S mm bed (250×210×220); inches scaling blows past bed by ~24×. Use mm.
- **Misread D**: assume Y axis needs flipping/mirroring to read text correctly (e.g. because print viewed from bed-underside). No evidence in data for mirroring — Marlin/Prusa toolpath coords are in the standard top-down bed frame the slicer generates from the model as oriented; you must render/plot the path top-down (X right, Y back) as-is and not apply a mirror unless you separately confirm the source model was mirrored.
- **Misread E**: assume S0 block boundaries alone (`M486 S0` … `M486 S-1`) give you only the text geometry cleanly separated from Shape-Box. Confirmed OK — object-scoped block data given (12 print blocks, 49918 G1 lines) is scoped strictly between `M486 S0` and the next `M486 S-1`, so isolating S0 blocks is valid; you must still union in interleaved G2/G3 lines within those same block boundaries (mechanical summary above only counted G1).
